Question:
A configured adjacency with accumulated failure history adopts a different exact winner that is already Established. Later a success callback from an older losing controller arrives. Which event can reset failure history, and why would cancelling a dial timer for a winner still in OpenConfirm have a different effect?

Key:
Required decisions: R1. Adoption of an already-established exact current winner performs the idempotent success reset; the stale old success cannot reset a newer history. R2. OpenConfirm winner ownership only suppresses dialing/clears scheduling authority while preserving accumulated history; scheduling cancellation is not establishment success.

PROBE A01

Question:
At a cleanup checkpoint the ledger has three reservations: P was revoked before its provider was invoked; Q was invoked and is still pending despite cancellation; R has settled but its owned result is awaiting disposal. Which reservations may be released now, and what condition releases each of the others?

Key:
Required decisions: R1. Only P can release now: revocation before invocation means no evaluation began. R2. Q remains reserved until settlement plus disposal; R remains reserved until disposal. Cancellation alone is not settlement, and an ended connection does not refund these reservations.

Rubric:

--- answer a4 ---
Decision: P may be released now, because its provider was never invoked. Q stays reserved until its provider actually settles and AGP disposes its retained request/result. Cancellation, revocation or the session ending does not release Q. R stays reserved while its result is waiting. Its slot is released once, when AGP actually disposes that owned result. In the terminal sequence, R counts as "actually disposable" work and can be released in that turn. Q cannot.

Inference or gap: The design does not say whether an ordinary (non-terminal) cleanup checkpoint must dispose R immediately or may defer it. It only says R is released on actual disposal.
